attempts.summary: On node1, nginx serves HTTPS on port 8443 using a certificate issued by a local self-signed CA. A systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, every 20s) runs renew-cert.sh, which checks the live cert with `openssl x509 -checkend 120` and, when it is within 120s of its 240s validity window, issues a fresh cert via issue-cert.sh (local CA, atomic file swap) and runs `systemctl reload nginx` to pick it up without dropping connections. This was demonstrated live: two automatic renewals (serial 1000→1001, then 1001→1002) occurred on schedule, each well before the prior cert's expiry, while a continuous curl loop (53 requests, one every ~2s) returned HTTP 200 throughout with zero failures, proving the service kept answering requests across the swap. The mandatory node-restart protocol was completed for the single managed node (node1): pre-restart boot_id and health baseline were captured, the node was rebooted via `systemctl reboot` (ack returned before disconnect, confirmed by a subsequent connection-refused poll), the boot_id changed post-restart, and nginx, the renewal timer, the cert files, and the renewal log all recovered — with a further automatic renewal (1001→1002) observed after reboot, confirming the auto-renewal pipeline persists across restarts. Final state: nginx and cert-renew.timer active/enabled, HTTPS on 8443 returning 200.
